paper1.title: WEST AFRICA AND THE WIDER WORLD FROM EARLIEST TIMES TO 2000

topics.title: Historiography and Historical Skills
topics.content: What is History and why do we study History? Sources of History; Historical skills (ancient and modern approaches); Prospect of ICT in historical studies.

topics.title: Trans-Saharan Trade
topics.content: Origin, organization and the effects on the development of West African states.

topics.title: European Contact with West Africa
topics.content: Reasons for their coming, immediate effects and West African reaction.

topics.title: Christian Missionary Activities in West Africa
topics.content: The suppression of slave trade. Christian Missionary activities and their impact on West Africa.

topics.title: The Scramble for and Partition of West Africa
topics.content: The Industrial Revolution, Scramble for colonies, Colonial subjugation, Occupation and West African reaction.

topics.title: Colonial Rule in West Africa
topics.content: Patterns of colonial rule, consolidation of European culture in Africa, colonial economy and the underdevelopment of Africa: colonial Africa and the two World Wars.

topics.title: Problems of Independent West African States
topics.content: Nature of politics: neo-colonialism and economic underdevelopment, unequal development within states and instability, the Military in West African politics, boundary disputes and threat to West African Unity.

topics.title: West Africa and International Organizations
topics.content: Membership, aims and objectives, achievements and failures of: (i) United Nations Organization (U.N.O.)/United Nations (U.N.); (ii) Organization of African Unity (O.A.U)/African Union (A.U.); (iii) Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS); etc.

paper2.title: NATIONAL HISTORIES OF THE GAMBIA, GHANA, LIBERIA, NIGERIA AND SIERRA LEONE UP TO 2000
paper2.note: Candidates answer questions on their home country only. Structured in Sections A, B, C with country-specific content.

topics: Historiography and Historical Skills
Origin, political, social and economic organization of major groups (Wollof, Mandinka, Fula, Jola, Krio(Aku), Serahuli)
Indigenous crafts and industries (Pottery, salt making, iron working, etc.)
Early European contact (Trade, Christianity and impact)
Introduction, spread and effects of Islam
The Gambia and the trans-Atlantic slave trade (Origin, organization and effects)
Suppression of the slave trade and its effects
The founding of Bathurst (Banjul)
Christian Missionary activities and their impact
The Soninke-Marabout wars, jihadist leaders
Resistance to European Colonialism (key figures)
British Colonial administration (Indirect Rule)
Economic and social developments in the colonial period (agriculture, transportation, education, health)
Development of local Government
The struggle for and regaining of independence (political parties, negotiations, Senegambia relations)
Development after independence (constitutions, coups, multiparty politics, Senegambia relations)
The Gambia and international organizations (UN, Commonwealth, AU, ECOWAS)

African pre-history up to 500 B.C.
